questions.q_en: P and Q start running in opposite directions on a circular track from the same point. If their speeds are 10 m/s and 8 m/s, respectively, then after what time will they meet if the length of the track is 1620 m?
questions.solution_en:
Relative speed of P and Q = Speed of P + Speed of Q

Relative speed = 10 + 8 = 18 m/s

Time taken to meet = Length of the track / Relative speed

=> 1620 / 18 = 90 seconds

questions.q_en: On a 2200 m long circular track, Sarita and Kavita drove their cycles from the same point but in opposite direction with the speeds 20 km/hr and 16 km/hr, respectively. After how much time will they meet again for the first time?
questions.solution_en:
Relative speed = 20 + 16 = 36 km/hr

= 36 X (1000 / 3600) = 10 m/s

Time to meet = circumference / relative speed = 2200 / 10 = 220 seconds

= 220 / 60 = 3 minutes + 40 seconds = 3 minutes 40 seconds

Option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
In a circular race of 840 m, A and B start running in the same direction at the same time from the same point at the speeds of 6 m/s and 12 m/s respectively. After how much time will they meet next?

Options:
questions.solution_en:
Given:

Circular track length = 840 m

Speed of A = 6 m/s

Speed of B = 12 m/s

Formula used:

Time to meet = Track length / Relative speed

Relative speed (since they are running in the same direction) = Speed of B - Speed of A

Calculation:

Relative speed = 12 m/s - 6 m/s = 6 m/s

Time to meet = 840 m / 6 m/s

=> Time to meet = 140 seconds

∴ A and B will meet next after 140 seconds

questions.q_en: In a circular race of 1600 m in length, Bhaskar and Vinay start with speeds of 27 km/h and 45 km/h starting at the same time from the same point. When will they meet for the first time on the track when running in the opposite directions and the same direction, respectively?
questions.solution_en:
(a) Opposite Directions:

Convert speeds to m/s:

  27 km/h = (27 X 5/18) = 7.5 m/s,

  45 km/h = (45 X 5/18) = 12.5 m/s.

Relative speed = 7.5 + 12.5 = 20 m/s.

Time = Distance / Relative Speed = 1600 / 20 = 80 seconds = 1 minute 20 seconds.

(b) Same Direction:

Relative speed = Difference = 12.5 - 7.5 = 5 m/s.

Time = 1600 / 5 = 320 seconds = 5 minutes 20 seconds.

Option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en: In a 1170 m race, Raman reaches the final point in 65 seconds and Mohan reaches the final point in 90 seconds. By how much distance does Raman beat Mohan?
questions.solution_en:
Speed of Mohan = 1170/90 = 13 m/s

Distance travelled by Mohan in 65 seconds = 13 * 65 = 845 m

Hence, required distance by which Reman beat Mohan = 1170 - 845 = 325 m

questions.q_en: Arvind and Chetan started running simultaneously from the same point in the same direction on a circular track of length 210 m. If Arvind takes 180 seconds to complete one round, and Chetan takes 420 seconds to complete one round, after how much time will they meet for the first time at the starting point on the track?
questions.solution_en:
Find LCM of 180 and 420.

Prime factorization of 180 = 22 X 32 X 5

Prime factorization of 420 = 22 X 3 X 5 X 7

LCM = 22 X 32 X 5 X 7

=> 4 X 9 X 5 X 7 = 1260 seconds

Convert 1260 seconds to minutes:

=> 1260 / 60 = 21 minutes

questions.q_en: In a circular race of 750 m, X and Y start from the same point and at the same time with speeds of 9 km/h and 13.5 km/h, respectively. If they are running in the same direction then, when will they meet again for the first time on the track?
questions.solution_en:
Speed of X=9 Km/h=9*5/18=2.5 m/sec

Speed of Y =13.5 km/h =13.5*5/18=3.75 m/sec

Relative speed when they run in same direction=

Speed of Y - speed of X

Relative speed = 3.75 - 2.5=1.25 m/sec

Given track length = 750 m

So they will meet again in :-

750/1.25=600 seconds.

Option (d) is the correct answer.

Speed of A = 36 X (1000/3600) = 10 m/s

Speed of B = 54 X (1000/3600) = 15 m/s

Relative speed (since they are running in opposite directions) = Speed of A + Speed of B

=> 10 + 15 = 25 m/s

Time when A and B will meet again = Length of the track / Relative speed

=> 4800 / 25 = 192 seconds

questions.q_en: A, B and C run simultaneously, starting from a point, around a circular track of length 1200m, at respective speeds of 2m/s, 4m/s and 6m/s. A and B run in the same direction, while C runs in the opposite direction to the other two. After how much time will they meet for the first time?
questions.solution_en:
Time taken by A to complete one round = 1200/2 = 600 sec

Time taken by B to complete one round = 1200/4 = 300 sec

Time taken by C to complete one round = 1200/6 = 200 sec

Time at which they will for the 1st time = LCM of 600, 300, and 200 = 600 sec

Hence, they will meet for the first after travelling for 600 sec or 10 min.

questions.q_en: Two runners, Sony and Mony, start running on a circular track of length 200 m at speeds of 18 and 24 km/h, respectively, in the same direction. After how much time from the start will they meet again at the starting point?
questions.solution_en:
Speed of Sony = 18 km/h = 5 m/s

Speed of Mony = 24 km/h = 20/3 m/s

Time taken by Sony to cover one round of the track = 200/5 = 40 sec

Time taken by Mony to cover one round of the track = 200/(20/3) = 30 sec

LCM of 40 sec and 30 sec = 120 sec

Hence, Sony and Mony will meet again at the starting point after travelling for 120 sec.

questions.q_en: A and B run a 12 km race on a circular track of length 1200 m. They complete one round in 300 seconds and 400 seconds, respectively. After how much time from start will the faster person meet the slower person for the last time?
questions.solution_en:
They will first time after the start of the race in (LCM of 300 and 400) seconds which is equal to 1200 seconds.

And they will keep meeting at an interval of 1200 seconds.

Time taken by faster person to complete the race = (12 * 1000)/1200 * 300 = 3000 seconds

They will meet for the 2nd time and last time after 2400 seconds from start. Because after 3000 seconds, A will finish the race.

questions.q_en: M and N walk along a circular track. They start at 5:00 a.m. from the same point in the opposite directions. M and N walk at a speed of 5 rounds per hour and 2 rounds per hour, respectively. How many times will they cross each other before 6.30 a.m. on the same day?
questions.solution_en:
As M and N are walking in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their speeds:

Relative Speed = Speed of M + Speed of N

Relative Speed = 5+2=7 rounds per hour

Time interval = 6:30 a.m.- 5:00 a.m. = 1.5 hours

Number of times they cross each other = Relative Speed x Time Duration

Number of times they cross each other =7 X 1.5

Number of times they cross each other = 10.5

Since they cannot cross each other half a time, we consider the whole number.

Number of times they cross each other before 6:30a.m. is 10.

Option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en: In a circular path of 600 m, Pankaj and Rohit start walking in opposite directions from the same point at the speeds of 2.85 m/s and 5.4 km/h, respectively. After how many minutes will they meet for the first time? (Rounded off to one decimal point)
questions.solution_en:
The speed of Pankaj = 2.85 m/s

The speed of Rohit = 5.4 km/h = 1.5 m/s

Let the distances covered by Pankaj and Rohit are 'd' m and (600 - d) m respectively.

Since, Pankaj and Rohit would have been covered the respective distances in same time.

So,

d/2.85 = (600 - d)/1.5

1.5d = 1710 - 2.85d

d = 1710/4.35

Now, the time, in which they will meet for the first time = 1710/(4.35 X 2.85)

= 138 seconds

= 2.3 minutes (approx.)

questions.q_en:
Varun and Sandeep started for a car race from the same point, in the same direction and at the same time on a circular track of length 1635 m with the speeds of 90 km/h and 108 km/h, respectively. After how much time (in seconds) will they meet again for the first time?

Options:
questions.solution_en:
Step 1: Calculate their relative speed.

· Speed of Varun = 90 km/h = 90 X 5/18 = 25 m/s

· Speed of Sandeep = 108 km/h = 108 X 5/18 = 30 m/s

· Relative speed = 30 - 25 = 5 m/s

Step 2: Time to meet again.

· They meet when the relative distance travelled equals the length of the track.

Time = Track Length/Relative Speed = 1,635/5 = 327 seconds

Thus, they will meet again after 327 seconds.

questions.q_en: Zeenat and Nasreen participate in a circular race of 1.2 km. They start the race at a speed of 18 km/h and 27 km/h, respectively, from the same point at the same time. After how much time (in minutes) will they meet at the starting point for the first time, if they are running in the same direction?
questions.solution_en:
Speed of Zeenat = 18 km/h = 18 * 5/18 = 5 m/s

Speed of Nasreen = 27 km/h = 27 * 5/18 = 7.5 m/s

Time taken by Zeenat to complete one round of the track = 1200/5 = 240 s

Time taken by Nasreen to complete one round of the track = 1200/7.5 = 160 s

Time (in seconds) after which they will meet for the first time at the starting time = LCM of 240 and 160 = 480 s

Time (in minutes) after which they will meet for the first time at the starting time = LCM of 240 and 160 = 480 s

= 8 minutes
